subject: SLA exception request for planned batch windows + proposed credit formula
messages:
From: Elaine Park <procurement@blueharbor.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA baseline & exception for nightly batch inference workload

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. BlueHarbor is excited about shifting more of our inferencing to Redwood, but we have one sticking point from procurement and ops: our nightly batch enrichment jobs (02:00–05:00 ET) are expected to spike tail-latency and we need a documented exception in the SLA to avoid over-penalizing Redwood for predictable processing windows.

Specifically we need:
- An explicit carveout window for scheduled batch processing where latency SLOs relax but availability remains intact.
- A clear monthly credit model that accounts for minutes below the agreed availability or latency thresholds during business hours (08:00–18:00 ET).

Our procurement team would prefer a simple baseline (e.g., 99.5% uptime) and a monthly credit schedule rather than an ambiguous "maintenance carveout". Can you send a proposed template exception (redline) and an example monthly credit calculation for our review? We also need to understand any hard caps on credits.

Attaching our internal note (referenced) — happy to hop on a call to work through numbers.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueHarbor Technologies
attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline & exception for nightly batch inference workload

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a proposal we think balances predictability for BlueHarbor and operational realities for Redwood. I attached a one-page draft (draft-sla-exception.pdf) you can use as a starting point.

Proposal (high level):
- Standard hosted SLA baseline: 99.9% monthly availability (no change).
- Exception carveout: For customers running scheduled batch inference in dedicated or reserved pools, we propose an "Operational Batch Window" definition and an alternate commitment: 99.5% availability and relaxed latency SLOs inside the documented batch window (default 02:00–05:00 ET). The idea is to account for expected higher p95 latency during heavy KV/cache churn.
- Latency SLO (business hours): p95 generation latency <= 250ms for production endpoints during 08:00–18:00 ET (applies outside the batch window).
- Monthly credit formula: credits (as percentage of monthly invoice) scale by weighted minutes below the availability threshold during business hours only. Example tiers:
  * < 0.5% monthly downtime: 0% credit
  * 0.5%–1.0%: 2% credit
  * 1.0%–2.0%: 5% credit
  * >2.0%: 8% credit
- Credit cap: Proposed 8% of monthly bill for this exception (we can negotiate a higher cap for Enterprise/Reserved deals).
- Notifications & scheduling: Customer must provide a minimum 14-day rolling schedule of planned batch windows; Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation report showing minutes in/out of the batch window and any latency incidents.

Notes/assumptions:
- The carveout only applies to latency SLOs; availability is still measured and eligible for credit per the formula above.
- Emergency rollbacks or unexpected hardware issues are addressed under standard maintenance carveouts in the master SLA.

Next steps: Laura, can you review for a legal/credit cap sanity check? Elaine, if this looks reasonable we can produce a redline (DocuSign link) and an example calculation for a $150k/month seat. I included a quick sample calculation in the attached PDF.

Attachments: draft-sla-exception.pdf (stub)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline & exception for nightly batch inference workload

Jordan — quick legal / product note from my side before we send a formal redline:

1) Cap: I recommend we increase the cap ceiling to 10% for negotiation flexibility, but hold 8% in the initial customer-facing proposal. We should include language allowing us to escalate to 10% with VP approval for strategic accounts.
2) Notification: Require 30 days' notice for any permanent change to announced batch patterns (14-day rolling is ok for recurring/temporary windows).
3) Auditability: Add requirement that BlueHarbor provide a short audit token (workload identifier + schedule) and allow Redwood to validate batch-window impact with our telemetry; this avoids disputes on whether an incident occurred inside/outside the carveout.
4) Example calculation: add a worked example for a $150k monthly invoice and show both percentage credit and absolute $ amounts.

I'll prepare a short legal redline and upload to DocuSign once Jordan confirms the preferred cap to show BlueHarbor. Karthik — any ops concerns on the scheduled validation approach?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <procurement@blueharbor.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueHarbor Legal <legal@blueharbor.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline & exception for nightly batch inference workload

Jordan / Laura — we reviewed internally and this is close to what we need. Two items from our side:

1) Business hours latency: can we tighten the p95 target to 200ms during 09:00–17:00 ET (core operating hours) rather than the 250ms window you proposed? That gives our support teams better predictability when supporting downstream services.
2) Credit cap: procurement prefers a 7% hard cap for this carveout; if Redwood can include a worked calculation (showing the math for $150k/mo) we can sign the exception faster.

If you can send an updated PDF redline and the DocuSign envelope, we'll target signature by EOW. HubSpot deal HS-4521 shows this is moving fast — I included a link below for your reference.

Regards,
Elaine Park
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueHarbor Technologies
